one_line_summary: A small review helper that traces a named function or symbol across several repositories and records the call path it found, so a reviewer can see whether a cross-repo route actually exists.
problem: In multi-repo codebases, a claim that one component reaches another often rests on a hop that has not been checked, and reviewers end up reading around rather than confirming the actual path.
audience: Strong engineering depth / code-review practice: people reviewing cross-module or cross-repo reachability who want a concrete trace record rather than an assertion.
solution: A tool that takes a start symbol and a target symbol, searches a set of repositories for definitions and references, records the path it actually found, and emits a trace with the files, lines, and unresolved hops. It is a review aid, not a full static analyzer.
key_features: Search a set of repositories for a named definition and for references to it
Record the chain of definitions and references between a start and a target
Mark unresolved hops explicitly instead of guessing
Emit a trace report with file paths, line anchors, and the status of each hop
Easy to run against a few repositories and easy to extend with another search backend
mvp_scope: A repository searcher that can find a symbol definition and its references in a small set of repositories, a trace builder that links them into a start-to-target chain, and a report emitter. The MVP covers plain functions/methods in a small set of repositories with a simple text- and AST-light search.
tests_plan: Unit tests for definition/references search over small synthetic repositories
Unit tests for trace construction and unresolved-hop marking
Unit tests for report formatting and anchor representation
